interactions.description: Concurrent use of Aspirin and Warfarin significantly increases the risk of major hemorrhage and gastrointestinal bleeding due to combined antiplatelet and anticoagulant actions.
interactions.concern: High risk of uncontrolled systemic or gastrointestinal bleeding.
interactions.action: Urgent review required. Avoid concurrent use unless specifically instructed and monitored by a cardiologist or hematologist with frequent INR checks.
interactions.source: FDA Safety Communication / Clinical Pharmacology Reference

interactions.description: Omeprazole significantly reduces the antiplatelet activity of Clopidogrel by inhibiting CYP2C19, the primary enzyme required to convert Clopidogrel to its active metabolite.
interactions.concern: Decreased cardioprotection and increased risk of recurrent thrombosis, heart attack, or stroke.
interactions.action: Avoid co-administration. Consider switching Omeprazole to Pantoprazole or an H2 blocker (e.g. Famotidine), which exhibits less CYP2C19 inhibition.
interactions.source: FDA Drug Safety Alert / ACCP Guidelines

interactions.description: Ibuprofen may competitively inhibit the cardioprotective antiplatelet effect of low-dose Aspirin and markedly compounds gastrointestinal ulceration risk.
interactions.concern: Loss of cardio-protective antiplatelet effect and amplified ulcer/bleeding risk.
interactions.action: Take immediate-release Aspirin at least 30 minutes before or 8 hours after Ibuprofen, or substitute Acetaminophen/Paracetamol for pain relief.

interactions.description: NSAIDs like Ibuprofen increase the anticoagulant effect of Warfarin and induce gastrointestinal mucosal damage, creating severe bleeding hazards.
interactions.concern: Severe gastrointestinal bleeding and elevated INR.
interactions.action: Avoid combination. Use Paracetamol for pain or fever under medical supervision.
interactions.source: American Heart Association / CHEST Antithrombotic Guidelines

interactions.description: NSAIDs inhibit renal prostaglandins, attenuating the antihypertensive effect of ACE inhibitors and escalating the risk of acute kidney injury and hyperkalemia.
interactions.concern: Loss of blood pressure control, renal deterioration, and elevated potassium levels.
interactions.action: Monitor blood pressure and serum creatinine/potassium closely. Limit NSAID duration or use alternative analgesic.

interactions.description: Concurrent use of ARBs (Losartan) and NSAIDs (Ibuprofen) may lead to acute renal impairment, especially in dehydrated or elderly patients, and blunts antihypertensive efficacy.
interactions.concern: Acute renal failure and reduced blood pressure reduction.
interactions.action: Ensure adequate hydration and monitor renal function. Prefer non-NSAID analgesics.

interactions.description: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors like Clarithromycin can dramatically elevate Atorvastatin plasma concentrations, increasing risk of rhabdomyolysis.
interactions.concern: Severe muscle pain, breakdown (rhabdomyolysis), and kidney failure.
interactions.action: Temporarily suspend Atorvastatin during antibiotic treatment or choose Azithromycin as an alternative.

interactions.description: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2 and CYP3A4, reducing Warfarin clearance and potentially eradicating vitamin K-producing gut flora.
interactions.concern: Dramatic elevation of INR and serious bleeding.
interactions.action: Frequent INR monitoring is mandatory. Warfarin dose adjustment typically required.

interactions.description: Co-administration of opioids and antihistamines can produce additive central nervous system (CNS) depression and psychomotor impairment.
interactions.concern: Excessive somnolence, dizziness, and decreased alertness.
interactions.action: Exercise caution when operating machinery or driving. Consider dose adjustments if excessive sedation occurs.

interactions.description: Cimetidine reduces renal clearance of Metformin, elevating systemic exposure and potential risk of lactic acidosis.
interactions.concern: Increased Metformin adverse effects and gastrointestinal intolerance.
interactions.action: Monitor blood glucose and signs of lactic acidosis. Consider alternative H2 receptor antagonist.

interactions.description: Amlodipine increases systemic exposure to Simvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism.
interactions.concern: Elevated statin levels and increased risk of myopathy.
interactions.action: Limit Simvastatin dose to 20 mg daily when co-administered with Amlodipine.

interactions.description: Dual blockade of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) with an ACE inhibitor and an ARB is generally contraindicated.
interactions.concern: Significantly increased risk of hypotension, hyperkalemia, and acute renal failure with no added clinical benefit.
interactions.action: Do not combine. Patient should be maintained on either an ACE inhibitor or an ARB, not both.

interactions.description: Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) confers synergistic platelet inhibition, increasing the incidence of major gastrointestinal and systemic bleeding.
interactions.action: Appropriate only under specific clinical indications (e.g. post-coronary stent or acute coronary syndrome) for an established duration with gastroprotection.

interactions.description: Co-administration of two systemic NSAID/antiplatelet agents significantly compounds gastrointestinal ulceration and renal toxicity.
interactions.concern: Gastrointestinal perforation, ulcers, and acute renal injury.

interactions.description: Simultaneous intake of two NSAIDs yields no additive therapeutic efficacy but substantially multiplies toxicities (ulcers, renal compromise, cardiac risk).
interactions.action: Discontinue one agent immediately in consultation with prescribing physician.
interactions.source: WHO Guidelines on Rational Drug Use
